_why: Advisories this tree carries that scripts/audit_gate.mjs will not fail the build on.
An entry is a DECISION, not a silence. It needs the reason it is survivable and the date it
gets looked at again. Past review_by the gate goes red on its own, and when upstream finally
publishes a patch the gate goes red asking for the entry to be deleted.
Everything here shares one fact, checked against the GitHub advisory API on 2026-08-19:
first_patched_version is NONE. There is no version of extract-zip or image-size, published
or unpublished, that resolves these. `npm audit fix --force` offers @lhci/cli@0.1.0, a
fourteen-major-version downgrade to a 2019 release, which is not a fix either.
What was NOT put on this list, because it was actually fixed: GHSA-ph9p-34f9-6g65 (tmp,
high) plus the external-editor and inquirer entries that hung off it. tmp was patched at
0.2.6 and this tree was on 0.0.33 and 0.1.0, so package.json overrides pins @lhci/cli's
subtree to ^0.2.7 and the advisory left the tree. Reach for that first, every time. This
file is for what is left after the fixing is done.

accepted.why: No patched version exists (vulnerable <= 2.0.1; 2.0.1 is the latest release, and the package has not shipped since 2020). It reaches us only through the devDependency @lhci/cli -> lighthouse -> puppeteer-core -> @puppeteer/browsers, which downloads a Chrome build from googlechromelabs.github.io and unzips it. The attack needs a hostile zip in that position, which means Google's download host is already serving one. Nothing in this chain touches a request, a customer or the built site: the only job that runs lhci is e2e-live-smoke.yml, after the deploy, against the live URL.
accepted.clears_when: extract-zip publishes a fix, or @puppeteer/browsers stops using it. Recheck both.

accepted.why: No patched version exists (vulnerable <= 2.0.2, which is the latest release). Denial of service via an infinite loop in the ICNS parser. It arrives through the devDependency @storybook/nextjs-vite -> vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs, which is not invoked by any workflow in .github/ and runs only when a developer types `npm run storybook` on their own machine. The input it would have to parse is an image already committed to this repo. A hang in a local Storybook is a developer restarting a process.
accepted.clears_when: image-size publishes a fix, or vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs drops it.

accepted.why: Same package, same chain and same reasoning as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr; this one is the JXL and HEIF parsers rather than ICNS. No patched version exists. Listed separately because the gate decides per advisory, so a fix for one must not silently cover the other.
accepted.clears_when: image-size publishes a fix, or vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs drops it.
